title: What Is a Prosthodontist?
seoTitle: What Is a Prosthodontist? vs Dentist & Periodontist
seoDescription: Prosthodontist vs periodontist vs general dentist: what each one does and when it matters, explained by board-certified prosthodontist Dr. Esam Nahlah.

text: Prosthodontist vs Periodontist vs General Dentist

A prosthodontist is a dentist who has trained for three more years in replacing and restoring teeth: implants, crowns, bridges, veneers and dentures. Here is how that differs from a general dentist and from a periodontist, and when it matters.
A prosthodontist rebuilds what is missing or broken.
Prosthodontics is one of the dental specialties recognized by the American Dental Association. Its work is

: dental implants, crowns, bridges, veneers, complete and partial dentures, and full-mouth rehabilitation. After dental school a prosthodontist trains for three more years in exactly this work, including the laboratory side of making it.
Dr. Esam Nahlah is board-certified by the American Board of Prosthodontics, a Diplomate since 2013, and a
Fellow of the American College of Prosthodontists
. He also teaches residents in the prosthodontics program at Virginia Commonwealth University, dentists in training to become prosthodontists.
Three kinds of dentist a patient with missing or failing teeth may meet, and what each one is trained for.
Your first call for most dental care.
A dentist who looks after everyday care for the whole family, and refers to a specialist when a case needs one.
The specialist in the gums and the bone around teeth.
Treats the tissues that hold teeth, and implants, in place: gum disease above all, and often implant placement.
Gum disease, from bleeding gums to advanced loss
The crown or arch on an implant often comes from another dentist
The specialist in replacing and restoring teeth.
Plans the finished teeth first, then works back to the implants, crowns or dentures that build them.
Trained in the laboratory work behind the teeth
Three years of specialty training after dental school
When a prosthodontist is worth seeing.
A general dentist handles most care well. These are the cases where the specialty earns its keep.
Implants, bridges or a full arch, planned from the finished teeth backwards, so the implants land where the teeth need them.
Dentures that will not stay put
A loose denture usually means receding bone. The fix is anchorage on implants, which a prosthodontist plans and restores.
A complex plan, or a second opinion
If another dentist called your case too complex, or quoted for implant surgery elsewhere, bring the plan and the scan: a second opinion here costs nothing.

faq: What is the difference between a prosthodontist and a periodontist?

A periodontist specializes in the gums and the bone that hold teeth, treating gum disease and often placing implants. A prosthodontist specializes in replacing and restoring the teeth themselves. At this practice the prosthodontist plans and places the implants and makes the teeth on them.
Is a prosthodontist better than a general dentist?

For everyday care, a general dentist is the right first call. For missing teeth, implants, dentures and full-mouth work, a prosthodontist has three more years of training in exactly that, which is why general dentists refer those cases to one.

What does board-certified mean for a prosthodontist?
That the prosthodontist has passed the examinations of the American Board of Prosthodontics and is a Diplomate of the Board. Dr. Nahlah became a Diplomate in 2013.
